Siegel Center]] |champion= |tourney= [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |tourney_result = Second Round }} {{2021–22 Atlantic 10 men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 VCU Rams men's basketball team''' represented [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They are led by fifth-year head coach is [[Mike Rhoades]] and played their home games at the [[Siegel Center]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]] as a member of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]]. They finished the season 22–10, 14–4 in [[2021–22 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|A-10 play]] to finish in a tie for second place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2022 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|A-10 tournament]], they lost in the quarterfinals to [[2021–22 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2021–22 Princeton Tigers men's basketball team|Princeton]] in the first round before losing to [[2021–22 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]]. ==Previous season== In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 VCU Rams men's basketball team|Rams]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 19–7, 10–4 in [[2020–21 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|A-10 play]] to finish in second place. In the [[2021 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|A-10 tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Dayton]]{{Cite web|title=Dayton vs. VCU - Game Summary - March 5, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401286894|access-date=2021-08-10|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} and [[2020–21 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]]{{Cite web|title=Davidson vs. VCU - Game Summary - March 6, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401286905|access-date=2021-08-10|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} to advance to the championship game where they lost to [[2020–21 St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball team|St. Bonaventure]].{{Cite web|title=St. Bonaventure wins A-10 tourney beating VCU for NCAA bid|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/03/14/st-bonaventure-wins-a-10-tourney-beating-vcu-for-ncaa-bid/115558694/|access-date=2021-08-10|website=USA TODAY|language=en-US}} VCU received an at-large berth to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 10 seed in the West region.{{Cite web|last=Davis|first=Marc|title=VCU earns at-large NCAA Tournament bid|url=https://www.nbc12.com/2021/03/14/vcu-earns-at-large-ncaa-tournament-bid/|access-date=2021-08-10|website=www.nbc12.com|language=en}} Due to several positive [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] tests in the VCU program prior to their First Round game against [[2020–21 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]], the game was declared a no-contest and Oregon advanced to the second round,{{Cite web|title=Oregon-VCU declared no-contest as COVID-19 positive advances Ducks into second round of 2021 NCAA Tournament|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/oregon-vcu-declared-no-contest-as-covid-19-positive-advances-ducks-into-second-round-of-2021-ncaa-tournament/|access-date=2021-08-10|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} making [[2020–21 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] the first team ever to forfeit a game in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|title=March Madness Is Hit With Its First Covid Forfeit|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/march-madness-covid-forfeit-vcu-ncaa-tournament-11616291101|website=Wall Street Journal}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
